name: Coastal and Marine Ecosystems of the Bijagós Archipelago – Omatí Minhô
subtitle: A natural property on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 2025.

parts.text: UNESCO describes the property in these words: “The property includes a continuous series of coastal and marine ecosystems, corresponding to the marine and intertidal environments of the best-preserved areas of the Bijagós Archipelago in Guinea-Bissau. The Archipelago is the only active deltaic archipelago on the African Atlantic coast and one of the few in the world. The site is home to a rich biodiversity, including endangered Green and Leatherback turtles, manatees, dolphins, and over 870,000 migratory shorebirds. It features mangroves, mudflats, and intertidal zones vital for marine life, and supports rare plant species, diverse fish populations, and bird colonies. Poilão Island is a globally important nesting site for turtles.”
The Bijagós are a group of about 88 islands and islets in the Atlantic off Guinea-Bissau. They formed from the ancient delta of the Geba and Grande de Buba rivers and cover 12,958 km².
Twenty of the islands are inhabited all year round. Bubaque is the most populated, and Bolama is the administrative capital.

The archipelago has mangroves, palm forests, dry forests and coastal savanna. It became a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 1996, and BirdLife International lists it as an Important Bird Area for waders, gulls, terns, flamingos and pelicans.
